title: What Survives a Change of Quantum Reference Frame? Coherence Thresholds for the Spectral, Holonomic, and Topological Content of Mixed-State Quantum Geometry
content: A reduced density matrix conditioned on an internal quantum reference frame (QRF) carries, through its mixed-state quantum geometric tensor, a Fisher–Bures metric and an Uhlmann gauge field. We determine which parts of this structure are frame independent, separating passive frame changes (reparametrizations and observer-local unitaries) from active ones (a change of the internal frame itself) within the perspective-neutral framework. Under passive changes the spectrum and the eigenbundle Chern numbers are invariant for every smooth single-valued transformation, the metric and the Uhlmann holonomy only for reparametrizations and constant unitaries. Under an active change between ideal frames the observer’s marginal obeys an exact shifted-overlap law for every relational state; its charge distribution is frame invariant, which gives the entanglement plus-coherence invariant of Cepollaro et al. in closed form. For a product relative state the law reduces to a partial twirl (relativization), under which the metric can only contract. For a two level observer the geometry is then graded by one inter-frame coherence |κ|: the Bures area is π|κ|, the Chern numbers survive for every |κ| > 0, and the equatorial Uhlmann Z2 holonomy only for |κ| > √3/2, the known thermal critical point reached here by coherence instead of temperature. For bounded generators the observer’s definability is itself frame relative.
